node_types.name: Service
node_types.definition: A deployable runtime component that handles requests, performs work, or coordinates other components

node_types.name: Store
node_types.definition: A persistent data store that holds state across requests and process lifetimes

node_types.name: ChainNode
node_types.definition: An external blockchain full or archive node that exposes the chain's native protocol (JSON-RPC, chain-sync, etc.) and is the source of truth for that chain's data

node_types.name: Client
node_types.definition: An external API consumer (developer's application) that calls the gateway over HTTP or WebSocket

nodes.definition: Stateless authenticated request entry: validates API keys and residency policy against auth_cache (with tenant_store as the canonical source on miss), enforces per-key rate limits via auth_cache and global throttle flags pushed by region_coordinator, records usage with usage_meter, routes RPC requests to chain_router and websocket subscriptions to fanout. Time-bucketed enforcement uses the hybrid logical clock from region_coordinator rather than wall-clock; observed inter-region clock skew above a threshold transitions the region into a documented degraded mode. Deployed in every region; no per-connection state outside auth_cache and fanout

Ethereum mainnet chain-node pool: a managed group of replicas with mixed roles — archive replicas (historical state, served on the historical-isolated path) and pruned tip replicas (current-state reads), preferably across diverse client implementations (Erigon + Geth) for byzantine cross-checking; chain_router and fanout select replicas from the pool

Sepolia testnet chain-node pool: a managed group of replicas mirroring the Ethereum pool's role split (archive + pruned tip), serving Sepolia mainnet's RPC and chain-sync interfaces; chain_router and fanout select replicas from the pool

Bitcoin chain-node pool: multiple Bitcoin Core replicas with txindex (archive role) plus pruned tip replicas, ZMQ notifications surfaced as chain-sync streams; chain_router and fanout select replicas from the pool

Cardano chain-node pool: multiple Cardano-node + Ogmios bridge replicas (archive + pruned tip roles), exposing chain-sync, local-state-query, and local-tx-monitor; chain_router and fanout select replicas from the pool

Canonical multi-region store of tenants, API keys, plan tiers, and rate-limit / quota state. Partitioned by tenant residency policy (tenant_store partitions are residency-scoped, not globally replicated for residency-pinned tenants). Concurrent writes resolve under an explicit policy: per-key single-writer in the tenant's home region for adds/updates, with global tombstoned revocations that any region observes regardless of replication direction (tombstones are not subject to last-write-wins). Each region holds the partitions it is allowed to host
External developer application that connects to the gateway over HTTP for request/response RPC and over WebSocket for real-time subscriptions

Public-facing untrusted-traffic filter: terminates TLS, applies IP-level rate limiting, runs WAF / bot-mitigation rules, and forwards only API-key-bearing traffic to the gateway. Routing is residency-aware: requests from a residency-pinned tenant (looked up via region_coordinator) are forwarded only to gateways in regions allowed by that tenant's policy, even when an out-of-policy region is closer by anycast. On reconnect storms (anycast flap, region drain), edge advertises jittered-backoff hints and regional affinity hints to clients so reconnect load spreads across surviving regions. Deployed at the network edge with anycast routing across regions

Per-chain routing service: receives authenticated RPC requests, selects a healthy replica from the region's chain pool, enforces per-tenant query cost budgets, isolates heavy historical queries onto the historical-replica subset, observes replica-level chain-head signals and reports them to region_coordinator (which computes the quorum-based canonical tip across all regions); for high-value reads against tip, it requires the canonical tip from region_coordinator rather than treating its region's pool as authoritative

Subscription multiplex layer: maintains the upstream chain-sync / newHeads / mempool subscriptions to each region's chain pools, publishes events to fanout_bus which subscriber-handling instances read from, multiplexes events to many client websockets, populates the per-chain address index, and emits explicit rollback notifications on reorg. Cursors are portable: each event is tagged with both an opaque cursor and a globally-meaningful chain coordinate (block number + intra-block index, or chain-stream sequence) so any region can replay from the cursor by reconstructing from the chain pool's history when its local ring buffer does not cover that coordinate. Canonical-tip and rollback decisions come from region_coordinator so subscribers reconnecting across regions see one canonical timeline. Event ordering exposed to subscribers uses chain-derived sequencing rather than wall-clock; the hybrid logical clock from region_coordinator is used only when chain ordering does not apply (e.g. cross-chain bookkeeping)

Per-chain index of recent block events keyed by address; populated by the fanout layer from each chain's block stream and read on every new block to match address-activity subscribers without scanning all subscriber filters

Per-region cache of tenant credentials, plan tier, residency policy, and rolling rate-limit / quota counters. Hydrated from tenant_store on miss, but throttle flags from region_coordinator (set when a tenant crosses any global ceiling) take precedence over and propagate ahead of fine-grained counter replication. Supports bulk hydration paths so a reconnect storm into a region does not produce an N-fold tenant_store read amplification

Per-tenant metering and accounting in each region: records request count, response bytes, chain-node CPU cost, and websocket egress against each API key; reports deltas to region_coordinator on a sub-second cadence so global cost ceilings and rate limits are enforced against globally-aggregated counters rather than region-local ones; detects anomalous per-key behaviour (geo, IP, request-pattern shifts) and surfaces alerts

Time-series store of per-tenant usage, error, latency, and rate-limit-headroom metrics with at least 30 days of retention; readable by tenants through the metrics API surfaced on the gateway. Sharded by residency policy: a residency-pinned tenant's metrics are physically located only in regions allowed by their policy

Per-region pub/sub multiplex layer that fanout publishes each upstream chain stream to and that subscriber-handling fanout instances read from to deliver to client websockets. Carries its own health, capacity budget, and failover policy. Region-local; cross-region delivery uses the canonical-tip + portable-cursor path on region_coordinator, not bus replication

Global control plane for multi-region semantics: (a) aggregates per-tenant quota and cost counters across regions on a sub-second cadence and propagates throttle flags ahead of fine-grained counter replication; (b) computes a single per-chain canonical-tip view by quorum across regional chain pools and emits coherent rollback notifications keyed on chain coordinates; (c) publishes each tenant's residency policy so edge, tenant_store, usage_meter, and metrics_store enforce it consistently; (d) distributes a hybrid-logical clock used by gateway and fanout in place of wall-clock for ordering and rate-limit bucketing. Logically a single global service; physically deployed as a quorum across regions so it is not itself a SPOF

requirements.description: System exposes Ethereum mainnet on-chain data (current and historical) to authenticated clients via the chain's native JSON-RPC interface
System exposes Sepolia testnet on-chain data (current and historical) to authenticated clients via the chain's native JSON-RPC interface
System exposes Bitcoin on-chain data (current and historical) to authenticated clients via the chain's native JSON-RPC interface
System exposes Cardano on-chain data (current and historical) to authenticated clients via the chain's native interface (Ogmios mini-protocols)
Clients can query state at any historical block on every supported chain (archive semantics, not just recent state)
Clients can subscribe over WebSocket and receive every new block header as it is observed by the corresponding chain node
Clients can subscribe over WebSocket and receive pending/unconfirmed transactions, including Cardano via the Ogmios local-tx-monitor mini-protocol
Clients can subscribe over WebSocket to a watched address and receive an event whenever that address sends or receives value on the corresponding chain
Every request and subscription is authenticated to a specific tenant via an API key looked up in the tenant store
Per-API-key request-rate limits and usage quotas are enforced before the request reaches a chain node
Each chain's native JSON-RPC / mini-protocol surface is exposed to clients without translation to a unified cross-chain schema
The system delivers reorg-safe semantics: WebSocket subscribers receive explicit rollback notifications, and REST/RPC responses can express finality status
For every supported chain, the system maintains multiple healthy chain-node replicas; failure of any single replica does not cause a client-visible error or subscription drop
Every chain-node replica is continuously health-checked; unhealthy replicas are excluded from the routing pool until they recover
Every chain has an explicit finality model and every emitted event carries the chain's confirmation depth and finality status at emission time
When a reorg occurs at any depth, subscribers receive an explicit rollback notification identifying the divergence point and a replay of the new canonical events
Subscribers can configure a per-stream confirmation threshold; events below the threshold are not delivered as confirmed
System supports at least 1M concurrent websocket subscribers per chain stream without per-process bottlenecks
Subscription fanout is decoupled from request handling; new subscribers do not degrade RPC request latency
System maintains a per-chain index of block events keyed by address so address-subscription matching scales sub-linearly in the number of subscribers
System enforces a per-request and per-tenant cost budget on chain queries; over-budget requests are rejected with guidance to chunk or use the historical pool
Long-running historical queries do not contend with tip-state requests on the same chain-node replica
Gateway caches tenant credentials and rate-limit state with explicit TTLs so a transient tenant_store outage does not cause a service outage
When tenant_store is unreachable, gateway operates in a documented degraded mode (cache-served auth, queued counter updates) and surfaces the degradation in metrics
Tenants can rotate API keys without service interruption (multiple active keys per tenant, immediate revocation, hot replacement)
System detects anomalous API-key usage (geo, IP, request-pattern shifts) and alerts the tenant
Pending-transaction events are emitted as transitions in a documented per-chain state machine (seen, replaced-by, dropped, confirmed) so subscribers can reason about non-monotonic mempool changes
Every event on a subscription stream carries an opaque cursor; clients can reconnect and request 'resume from cursor X' to replay missed events within a documented retention window
Untrusted public traffic is filtered at an edge layer (TLS termination, IP rate-limit, WAF, bot mitigation) before it reaches the gateway's chain-bound code paths
Every supported chain has a documented upgrade procedure that pre-stages new node/bridge versions and transitions traffic across forks without a client-visible outage
Every subscription and response surface advertises a protocol/schema version so client code can detect and negotiate compatible behaviour across chain upgrades
System runs active-active in at least two independent regions; failure of any one region does not cause a global outage and clients reconnect into a surviving region without manual intervention
tenant_store state is replicated across regions with bounded lag; each region can authenticate and rate-limit using local replicas
System measures per-tenant cost drivers beyond request count (chain-node CPU, response bytes / egress) and attributes them to the tenant in near-real-time
Each tenant plan has explicit monthly cost ceilings; approaching the ceiling triggers warnings, crossing it triggers throttle/reject with a clear error
Tenants can read per-key usage, error, latency, and rate-limit-headroom metrics for at least the past 30 days through a metrics API
System cross-checks chain head and canonical block hashes across multiple chain-node replicas and quarantines any replica that diverges from the consensus tip
Where a chain has multiple production-quality client implementations, the chain-node pool includes more than one implementation to bound client-bug blast radius
Per chain, the system supports tiered storage (hot recent state, cold deep archive with on-demand re-warming) so storage cost grows sub-linearly with chain history
For tip-state requests, the chain pool can include pruned (non-archive) replicas; tip-state read capacity scales independently of archive storage

Per-tenant quota and cost-ceiling enforcement aggregates counters across all regions on a bounded sub-second cadence so that overshoot is bounded by aggregation latency, not by tenant_store replication lag

When a tenant crosses a global cost or rate ceiling, a throttle flag propagates to every region's auth_cache faster than fine-grained counter replication, so subsequent requests in any region are rejected immediately

Concurrent writes to tenant_store across regions resolve under an explicit, documented conflict-resolution policy (CRDT, partition by tenant home region, or write quorum) so that no key revocation can be 'un-revoked' by a conflicting concurrent write
Key and tenant revocations are stored as tombstones with global ordering so any region's auth_cache hydration sees a revocation regardless of replication lag direction

Subscription cursors are portable across regions: a cursor issued in region A can be resumed from in region B, and the system reconstructs missed events from a globally-meaningful coordinate (chain block + offset or a chain-stream sequence) when the local ring buffer does not cover the requested cursor

For each supported chain, the system advertises a single canonical-tip view across all regions, computed by quorum across regional chain pools, so that the canonical chain history a subscriber sees is independent of which region they connect to

When a reorg is detected, the rollback notification carries a globally-meaningful divergence point (chain coordinate, not region-local cursor) so all regions emit a coherent rollback to their subscribers regardless of when each region's chain pool observes the reorg

Cross-region event ordering exposed to subscribers is derived from chain-native sequencing (block + intra-block index, or chain-stream sequence) rather than gateway wall-clock, so cross-region clients see the same ordering regardless of inter-region clock skew

Rate-limit windows and other time-bucketed enforcement use a hybrid-logical or coordinated clock that bounds inter-region skew explicitly; observed skew above a threshold puts the affected region into a documented degraded mode

Each tenant has an explicit residency policy that constrains the regions in which their tenant data, traffic, and derived telemetry may live; the system enforces this policy at the edge, in tenant_store partitioning, and in metrics_store / usage_meter sharding

Edge routing is residency-aware: requests from a residency-pinned tenant are forwarded only to gateways in regions allowed by that tenant's policy, even when an out-of-policy region is closer by anycast

When connections drop en masse (anycast flap, region drain, edge restart), the system bounds the reconnect-storm load on surviving regions through advertised jittered-backoff hints, bulk auth_cache hydration paths, and pre-warmed fanout state for the most likely failover regions

The internal pub/sub layer that fanout uses to multiplex chain streams is modeled as an explicit component with its own health, capacity, and failover semantics, so its failure modes are visible to operators and to stress testing

satisfactions.explanation: eth_archive is an Ethereum mainnet archive node serving the chain's native JSON-RPC; the gateway proxies authenticated requests to it
sepolia_archive is a Sepolia testnet archive node serving the chain's native JSON-RPC; the gateway proxies authenticated requests to it
btc_archive is a Bitcoin Core full node with txindex; the gateway proxies authenticated requests to its JSON-RPC and notification interface
ada_archive is a Cardano node + Ogmios bridge exposing chain-sync, local-state-query, and local-tx-monitor; the gateway proxies authenticated requests to it
All four chain nodes are configured in archive mode (or with full history), so historical state at any block is reachable through their native interfaces
The gateway opens a long-lived chain-sync / newHeads subscription against each chain node and forwards new headers to subscribed websocket clients
The gateway subscribes to each chain node's pending-transaction stream (eth newPendingTransactions, btc ZMQ rawmempool, ada Ogmios local-tx-monitor) and forwards pending txs to subscribed clients
The gateway evaluates each new block and pending-tx event against client-supplied address filters and pushes a match event to the relevant subscribers
The gateway resolves the API key on every connection/request against tenant_store and tags the session with the tenant identity
The gateway updates per-key rate-limit and quota counters in tenant_store on each request and rejects requests that exceed the tenant's configured limits
The gateway forwards JSON-RPC method calls verbatim per chain (eth_*, btc getblock/getrawtransaction/etc., Ogmios mini-protocols) without rewriting them into a common schema

The gateway tracks rollback events emitted by each chain node's chain-sync/newHeads stream and forwards them as explicit rollback messages on the matching websocket subscriptions; REST responses include the chain head's finality at request time

Each chain pool (eth_archive, sepolia_archive, btc_archive, ada_archive) is now defined as a managed group of replicas; chain_router selects from healthy replicas, so single-replica failure is invisible to clients
chain_router's replica-selection policy continuously health-checks pool members and excludes unhealthy ones until they recover
fanout tags every emitted event with the source chain's confirmation depth and finality status before delivery
fanout subscribes to chain pools' chain-sync streams, observes rollbacks, and emits explicit rollback notifications + canonical replay through its multiplex layer
Subscriptions accepted by the gateway carry a confirmation-threshold parameter; fanout filters events below the threshold per stream
The dedicated fanout service is horizontally scalable; a single chain stream is consumed once and multiplexed via internal pub/sub to many subscriber-handling fanout instances
Subscription state lives in the fanout service, not the gateway, so RPC request handling on the gateway is unaffected by subscriber count
fanout populates address_index keyed by address as it processes each block; address-activity subscribers register at the index and only receive matched events
chain_router enforces per-tenant query-cost budgets (request and monthly), rejecting or chunking over-budget requests with explicit guidance
chain_router routes long-running historical queries to the archive subset of each chain pool, separated from the pruned-tip subset that serves tip-state requests
auth_cache (a gateway-local Store) holds tenant credentials and rate-limit state with explicit TTLs, populated from tenant_store and consulted on every authenticated request

When tenant_store is unreachable on cache miss, gateway operates in a degraded mode using the existing auth_cache entries; usage_meter queues counter updates for replay; degradation surfaces as a metric
tenant_store models multiple active keys per tenant with revocation timestamps; gateway/auth_cache honour revocation immediately on TTL refresh
usage_meter tracks per-key behavioural baselines (geo, IP, request pattern) and flags anomalies into metrics_store and tenant alerts
fanout normalises each chain's mempool semantics into a documented pending-tx state machine (seen / replaced-by / dropped / confirmed) and emits state-transition events
fanout assigns an opaque cursor to every emitted event and retains a per-chain ring buffer; clients reconnecting can request 'resume from cursor X' within the documented retention window
edge service terminates TLS, applies IP rate-limiting, runs WAF + bot-mitigation rules, and only forwards API-key-bearing traffic to the gateway

Each chain pool's definition allows replica replacement; pre-fork upgrade pre-stages new replicas in the pool, gradually shifts traffic via chain_router/fanout, and retires old versions after the fork window
gateway, chain_router, and fanout advertise a protocol/schema version on every subscription handshake and RPC response so client code can detect breaking changes

edge anycasts traffic across regions; gateway, chain_router, fanout, auth_cache, address_index, usage_meter, and metrics_store are deployed per region; clients reconnect into a surviving region transparently
tenant_store is now defined as multi-region replicated, with each region holding a local replica readable by gateway and usage_meter
usage_meter receives per-request signals from gateway and chain_router (request count, chain-node CPU estimate, response bytes, websocket egress) and attributes them per tenant in near-real-time
usage_meter enforces monthly per-tenant cost ceilings; approaching the ceiling emits warnings, crossing it triggers throttle/reject decisions enforced by gateway and chain_router via auth_cache flags

usage_meter writes per-tenant usage, error, latency, and rate-limit-headroom metrics to metrics_store with at least 30 days of retention; the gateway exposes a metrics API that reads from metrics_store
chain_router cross-checks chain heads and canonical block hashes across multiple replicas in each pool, quarantining divergent replicas via the same health-check path
Each chain pool's definition explicitly admits multiple client implementations (e.g. Erigon + Geth for Ethereum) to bound client-bug blast radius
Each chain pool's definition includes both archive replicas (cold deep history) and pruned replicas (hot recent state); chain_router routes queries to the appropriate tier
Each chain pool's definition explicitly includes pruned tip-only replicas; chain_router routes tip-state requests to them, scaling tip-read capacity independently of archive storage

usage_meter reports per-tenant deltas to region_coordinator on a sub-second cadence; region_coordinator aggregates them globally and bounds overshoot to aggregation latency rather than tenant_store replication lag

region_coordinator writes_to auth_cache: when any region's aggregated counter crosses a global ceiling, region_coordinator pushes a throttle flag into every region's auth_cache, propagating ahead of fine-grained counter replication

tenant_store is redefined with per-key single-writer in the tenant's home region for adds/updates plus globally-tombstoned revocations, so concurrent writes resolve under an explicit policy that cannot un-revoke a key
tenant_store tombstones revocations globally and any region's auth_cache hydration sees the tombstone regardless of replication direction

fanout's redefinition tags every event with a globally-meaningful chain coordinate alongside the opaque cursor; replay can be served from any region by reconstructing from the chain pool's history when its local ring buffer doesn't cover the requested coordinate

region_coordinator computes a single per-chain canonical-tip view by quorum across regional chain pools (chain_router calls region_coordinator with head observations); fanout and chain_router consult region_coordinator for the canonical tip

region_coordinator emits rollback notifications keyed on globally-meaningful chain coordinates; fanout in every region forwards the same coherent rollback regardless of when its local chain pool observed the reorg
fanout's redefinition specifies that subscriber-visible ordering uses chain-derived sequencing (block + intra-block index, or chain-stream sequence), not gateway wall-clock

gateway uses the hybrid logical clock distributed by region_coordinator for time-bucketed enforcement; gateway's redefinition specifies a degraded mode when observed inter-region skew crosses a threshold

tenant_store partitions are residency-scoped; region_coordinator publishes each tenant's residency policy to edge, gateway, usage_meter, and metrics_store; metrics_store and usage_meter are sharded by residency

edge's redefinition specifies residency-aware routing: edge calls region_coordinator to look up the tenant's residency policy and forwards only to gateways in allowed regions, even when a closer region is anycast-eligible

edge advertises jittered-backoff and regional-affinity hints on disconnect; auth_cache supports bulk hydration paths (per its redefinition); region_coordinator's throttle/quota state lets surviving regions absorb the reconnect storm without N-fold tenant_store amplification

fanout_bus is now an explicit Store node in the spec with its own definition (health, capacity budget, failover policy); fanout writes_to and reads_from fanout_bus, so the multiplex layer is visible to operators and stress testing
